builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Low-rank corrections to a shared reference Jacobian for GPU-parallel AC $N\!-\!1$ contingency analysis
summary: The technique replaces per-topology sparse refactorization of the Jacobian with a single reference matrix inversion and low-rank Woodbury corrections for topology changes. It requires implementing a Newton--Raphson solver with inner iterative methods (truncated Neumann or BiCGStab) and storing the inverted reference matrix plus correction factors. The approach can fail if the spectral radius of the iteration matrix exceeds unity or if the condition number makes the reference Jacobian an ineffective preconditioner for specific outage scenarios.
rationale: This method addresses a power systems engineering problem outside the AI/ML domain and provides no transferable technique for improving model inference, training, or agent systems on the reader's infrastructure.
technique: Low-rank Woodbury correction for GPU-parallel contingency analysis

claims.statement: The technique replaces per-topology sparse refactorization of the Jacobian with a single reference matrix inversion and low-rank Woodbury corrections for topology changes. It requires implementing a Newton--Raphson solver with inner iterative methods (truncated Neumann or BiCGStab) and storing the inverted reference matrix plus correction factors. The approach can fail if the spectral radius of the iteration matrix exceeds unity or if the condition number makes the reference Jacobian an ineffective preconditioner for specific outage scenarios.
Per-topology solve times competitive with an optimized 80-core CPU baseline, with the low-rank correction accounting for approximately 1-2% of the workload.
